sections.1.heading: What Express Invoice is good at
sections.1.body:
People searching for an **Express Invoice alternative** usually started with the free version and then outgrew it. It helps to be fair about what Express Invoice does well first. According to [NCH's product page](https://www.nchsoftware.com/invoice/index.html), checked on 28 November 2026:

- **It runs on your computer,** on Windows 7 to 11 and on macOS, with mobile apps for Android and iPhone.
- **The free version doesn't expire.** It's for home users or businesses with one user, and includes most of the paid version's features.
- **It covers more than invoices,** including quotes, orders, recurring invoices, payment reminders and statements for overdue accounts.
- **It works offline,** so you can create invoices when the internet is down.
- **It handles several businesses,** multiple tax rates and multiple currencies.

The page doesn't list prices for the paid version, and we couldn't confirm them, so we don't quote them here.

What the page doesn't mention is time tracking. Express invoicing software is built for typing invoice lines, such as items, quantities and prices. For a business that sells products or fixed services, that's exactly right.
sections.2.heading: Where a team that bills hours gets stuck
sections.2.body:
The trouble starts when the business grows from one person to a team that bills by the hour. Three problems tend to appear together.

**The free version stops fitting.** It's for one user. Once several people need to work in it, the free version is no longer the right tool, and you need to look at the paid version or something else.

**Hours live somewhere else.** Without time tracking, each person keeps hours in a spreadsheet, a notebook or another app. At month end, someone collects them, multiplies by the right rates and types the totals into invoice lines. Every step is a chance to miss an hour or apply the wrong rate.

**It's tied to one computer.** Desktop software suits a single person at a single desk. NCH offers web access to the desktop version, but a team working from several places usually wants a tool everyone signs into directly.

If none of these sound familiar, Express Invoice may be all you need, especially if you rely on its quotes, recurring invoices or offline mode, which Paidlyo doesn't have. For a wider look at the options, see our guide to [free invoicing software](/guides/is-there-any-free-invoicing-software).
sections.3.heading: How Paidlyo handles the same month
sections.3.body:
Here's a month of billing for a 3-person bookkeeping and advisory practice, first the typical Express Invoice way and then in Paidlyo.

### Without time tracking

Each person logs hours in a spreadsheet. On the last day of the month, the owner collects three spreadsheets, sorts the hours by client, applies the rate for each kind of work and types the lines into each invoice. For 12 clients, that's 12 invoices built by hand.

### In Paidlyo

Each person tracks time with the timer or the weekly timesheet, picking the client, project and task. Rates are set once: $95 an hour for bookkeeping and $160 for advisory work.

At month end, the owner opens a client's unbilled time:

| Task | Hours | Rate | Amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monthly bookkeeping | 9 | $95 | $855 |
| Advisory call and follow-up | 2.5 | $160 | $400 |
| Total | 11.5 | | $1,255 |

One click creates the invoice draft with those lines. The owner checks it, adds tax, and shares a private link. The client opens it without an account and can save a PDF.

For 12 clients, the owner repeats this 12 times, but each one takes a quick check rather than a build from scratch. If a client disputes an hour, the entry is there with its date, person and task.

The difference isn't the invoice itself. Both tools produce a clean, branded invoice. The difference is that the hours, rates and totals are already there.
sections.3.callout: Before switching, count how long last month's invoices took to build. It tells you whether the change is worth paying for.
sections.4.heading: What this Express Invoice alternative doesn't do
sections.4.body:
An honest comparison should list what you'd give up. Compared with Express Invoice, Paidlyo has:

- **No free version.** Paidlyo costs $9 per person a month after a 14-day trial.
- **No quotes, orders or recurring invoices.** Paidlyo creates invoices from tracked time, and you can edit each draft.
- **No offline mode.** It runs in the browser, so you need a connection.
- **No mobile apps.** You can open it in a browser, but there's no app to install.
- **No online card payments.** You record full or partial payments yourself.
- **No inventory or product catalogue.** It's built for time, not stock.

Paidlyo does include things that matter for hourly work: rates per project and per task, project budgets, billable and non-billable hours, reports on hours by client, project and task, an unbilled time report, and an outstanding invoices report by age. Everything can be exported to CSV.

If most of what you invoice is products, recurring fees or quotes that turn into orders, Express Invoice is likely the better tool. If most of what you invoice is your team's time, Paidlyo removes the step of turning hours into invoice lines. Our guide on [what invoicing software does](/guides/what-is-invoicing-software) explains the main types.
sections.5.heading: Switching from Express Invoice
sections.5.body:
There's no import from Express Invoice, so the move is a clean start. For a small team it takes an afternoon:

1. **Pick a start date,** such as the first of next month.
2. **Keep Express Invoice for older invoices** until the unpaid ones are paid, so you don't move open balances by hand.
3. **Add your active clients** in Paidlyo, with each client's currency, and upload your logo.
4. **Create projects and tasks** with your hourly rates, and budgets where clients have a cap.
5. **Invite the team** and ask everyone to track time from the start date.
6. **Create the first invoices** from unbilled hours at the end of the month.

Keep a copy of your Express Invoice data on your computer for your records. Paidlyo's reports and CSV export will cover everything from your start date.

Paidlyo costs $9 per person a month, or $90 per person a year, with unlimited clients, projects and invoices. A card is needed to start the 14-day trial, and nothing is charged until it ends. Read more about [creating invoices in Paidlyo](/invoicing).

sections.1.heading: When a Sage invoicing alternative makes sense
sections.1.body:
Most people looking for a **Sage invoicing alternative** are happy with Sage for bookkeeping. The friction is the hourly side. Sage invoicing software sits inside Sage Accounting, a full accounting product built for bookkeeping, VAT and financial reports. Billing a team's hours is not its main job.

Sage's plans and prices vary by country, so check your local pricing page. Two examples, checked on 28 November 2026:

- **South Africa:** [Sage's pricing page](https://www.sage.com/africa/sage-business-cloud/accounting/pricing/) lists Accounting Start at R3,240 a year including VAT for 1 user, and Accounting Standard at R5,880 a year with 2 users included and up to 5. Extra users cost R85 a month each, and **Time Tracking is an add-on at R185 a month**. Multi-currency payments are another R185 a month.
- **United Kingdom:** [Sage's UK pricing](https://www.sage.com/en-gb/pricing/) describes Accounting Standard at £43 a month, and Accounting Plus at £59 a month with multi-currency and unlimited users.

So a South African agency that wants time tracking and foreign-currency invoices pays for two add-ons on top of its plan, plus a fee for each user beyond the plan's allowance.

One thing to be clear about: Paidlyo has **no Sage integration**. It doesn't send invoices or hours to Sage. It's an alternative for hourly billing, not an add-on to your books.
sections.2.heading: Who should stay on Sage
sections.2.body:
Sage Accounting does much more than Paidlyo, and for many businesses it's the right place to invoice. Stay with Sage if:

- **Your accountant works in Sage** and wants every invoice in the ledger the moment it's created.
- **You need bookkeeping,** such as bank feeds, bills, expenses and financial reports. Paidlyo has none of these.
- **You submit VAT returns from Sage.** Paidlyo doesn't calculate or submit VAT returns.
- **You sell products or fixed fees** more than hours, or rely on quotes and inventory.
- **People need a mobile app.** Sage lists mobile apps; Paidlyo runs only in the browser.

Paidlyo makes more sense when hourly billing is the core of the business: several people track time for clients, each kind of work has its own rate, projects have budgets, and you want to see unbilled hours before month end. In that case, Sage stays as the books and Paidlyo handles the hours and the invoices built from them.

If you're still deciding between a dedicated billing tool and an accounting package, our guide on [what invoicing software is](/guides/what-is-invoicing-software) explains the main types and what each is good at.

sections.3.heading: A month of billing with Paidlyo and Sage
sections.3.body:
Here's how a 4-person consultancy might bill one client for a month using Paidlyo for hours and Sage for the books.

The team tracks time in Paidlyo with the timer or the weekly timesheet. Each entry has a client, a project, a task and a billable flag. Rates are set on the project: senior advice at $150 an hour, analysis at $95 and meetings at $95.

At month end, the owner opens the client's unbilled time and creates an invoice grouped by task:

| Task | Hours | Rate | Amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| Senior advice | 14 | $150 | $2,100 |
| Analysis | 38 | $95 | $3,610 |
| Meetings | 6 | $95 | $570 |
| Total before tax | 58 | | $6,280 |

The owner checks the draft, adds tax, and shares a private link. The client opens it without an account and can save a PDF.

Then the routine continues in Sage:

1. **Record the invoice in Sage** with the Paidlyo invoice number and total, so the income is in the books.
2. **When the client pays,** record the payment in Paidlyo so the outstanding invoices report stays correct, and in Sage against the invoice.
3. **At month end,** export outstanding invoices from Paidlyo to CSV, so your bookkeeper can check both systems agree.

For a business sending 10 to 30 invoices a month, the extra recording takes a short session. For a business sending hundreds, the double entry adds up, and invoicing directly in Sage with its time tracking add-on is likely the better choice.
sections.4.heading: Comparing the cost
sections.4.body:
A direct price comparison is tricky, because Sage prices by country and currency, and its plans include bookkeeping that Paidlyo doesn't. Instead, look at what you'd actually pay for hourly billing in each setup.

**Setup A: Sage only.** Your plan, plus the Time Tracking add-on where your region charges for it, plus multi-currency if you bill foreign clients, plus a fee for each user beyond the plan's allowance. Using the South African prices above, a team of 5 on Accounting Standard would pay for 3 extra users and both add-ons each month on top of the plan.

**Setup B: Sage for the books, Paidlyo for hours and invoices.** Your Sage plan without the time and currency add-ons, and possibly fewer Sage users, because only the people who do bookkeeping need a Sage login. Plus Paidlyo at $9 per person a month for everyone who tracks time.

**Setup C: Paidlyo plus a different bookkeeping tool or an accountant.** Paidlyo for hours and invoices, and your accountant keeps the books from your exports.

Which is cheapest depends on your team size and your local prices. Write down what you'd pay in each setup for your real team before deciding. Paidlyo's yearly plan is $90 per person a year. Our guide on [how much invoicing software costs](/guides/how-much-does-invoicing-software-cost) compares more pricing models.
sections.5.heading: Starting with Paidlyo
sections.5.body:
There's no import from Sage, and you don't need one if Sage stays your bookkeeping system. To start billing hours in Paidlyo:

1. **Agree the monthly routine** with your accountant: who records Paidlyo invoices in Sage, and which system is the record for payments.
2. **Add your active clients** with their currency, and upload your logo.
3. **Create projects and tasks** with hourly rates, and budgets where you've agreed them with clients.
4. **Invite the team** as members, with admins for anyone who manages billing.
5. **Track a full month,** then create invoices from unbilled hours and record them in Sage.
6. **Stop creating hourly invoices in Sage** from that month, so nothing is billed twice.

After the first cycle, check the unbilled time report to make sure every billable hour reached an invoice. If you used Sage's time tracking add-on, you can cancel it once the team is tracking in Paidlyo.

Paidlyo costs $9 per person a month, with every feature included and unlimited clients, projects and invoices. The 14-day trial is long enough to set up and test with real work; a card is needed to start, and nothing is charged until it ends. Read more about [billable hours in Paidlyo](/features/billable-hours).

sections.1.heading: When to look for a Bonsai alternative

Teams usually look for a **Bonsai alternative** for one of two reasons. Either they use only a small part of what Bonsai offers and the price feels high for that part, or the team has grown and per-seat costs on the plan they need have added up.

Bonsai is an all-in-one tool. According to [Bonsai's pricing page](https://www.hellobonsai.com/pricing), checked on 28 November 2026, its plans are priced per user:

| Plan | Monthly | Billed yearly | Main additions |
|---|---|---|---|
| Basic | $15 | $9 | Time tracking, tasks, projects, CRM, mobile apps |
| Essentials | $25 | $19 | Invoices and payments, proposals, contracts, client portal, expenses |
| Premium | $39 | $29 | Workload, Gantt, profit reports, QuickBooks and Xero |
| Elite | $59 | $49 | Custom permissions, timesheet locking; 3-user minimum |

The key detail for hourly businesses: **Basic includes time tracking but not invoicing.** To create invoices, you need Essentials or above. So a team that tracks hours and bills them starts at $25 per user a month, or $19 on yearly billing.

Paidlyo does a narrower job, team time tracking and invoices from tracked time, for $9 per person a month, or $90 per person a year, with every feature on one plan.
sections.2.heading: Who should stay on Bonsai
sections.2.body:
Bonsai covers far more of the client lifecycle than Paidlyo, and for many freelancers and small agencies that's exactly the point. Stay with Bonsai if you rely on:

- **Proposals and contracts.** Sending a proposal, getting it signed and turning it into a project in one tool is genuinely useful. Paidlyo has neither.
- **Online payments.** Bonsai lists online payments on invoices from Essentials. Paidlyo doesn't take payments; you record them yourself.
- **A client portal and forms.** Paidlyo shares each invoice as a no-login link, but has no portal.
- **CRM and a deals pipeline,** for tracking leads before they become clients.
- **Mobile apps** for tracking on the go. Paidlyo runs only in a browser.
- **QuickBooks or Xero sync,** on Premium and up. Paidlyo has no accounting integration.
- **Expense tracking** to rebill clients.

If you use three or more of these regularly, Bonsai's price is buying real value, and a narrower tool would leave gaps you'd need to fill with other apps.

Paidlyo makes sense when most of that list goes unused, and what your team actually does every day is track hours, apply rates, watch budgets and bill clients at month end.

- **Team:** $8.50 per seat a month billed yearly, with a **minimum of 5 seats**. It includes all features: native integrations, billing, budgeting and invoicing, SSO and advanced permissions.

The page shows the Team price for yearly billing; a monthly option exists, but its price isn't listed. Annual payment saves 15%, and unused months aren't refunded. There's a 14-day trial with all features and no card.

- **Your team lives in Asana, Jira, ClickUp or a similar tool.** Everhour lists 40+ integrations and is built to add time tracking inside those tools. Paidlyo has no integrations; time is tracked in Paidlyo itself.
- **You need expenses or time off** alongside time tracking. Both are listed as Everhour features. Paidlyo has neither.
- **You have 5 or more people and want a free start.** Everhour's free plan covers up to 5 seats for basic tracking. Paidlyo has no free plan.
- **You need SSO or advanced permissions.** Paidlyo has three roles: owner, admin and member.

**Paidlyo is the better fit if:**

- you're a team of 1 to 4 who'd otherwise pay for empty seats;
- you don't use a project management tool, or you'd rather keep time tracking separate from it;
- you want invoices built from unbilled time, rates per project and task, budgets and outstanding invoice reports in one simple tool;
- you'd like the option to pay monthly at a clear price.

If you do use a project tool and want time tracked inside it, Everhour's integrations are a real advantage. Our page on [Paidlyo as a ClickUp time tracking alternative](/alternatives/clickup) explains the trade-offs of keeping time separate.
sections.2.callout: Count your seats honestly. If your team will grow past 5 within a year, the minimum matters less than features and how people prefer to track.
sections.3.heading: What small teams pay
sections.3.body:
Here's how the seat minimum affects real team sizes, using Everhour's yearly Team price and Paidlyo's prices:

| Team size | Everhour Team, yearly | Paidlyo, yearly | Paidlyo, monthly |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 person | $510 a year (5 seats) | $90 a year | $9 a month |
| 2 people | $510 a year (5 seats) | $180 a year | $18 a month |
| 4 people | $510 a year (5 seats) | $360 a year | $36 a month |
| 10 people | $1,020 a year | $900 a year | $90 a month |

Below 5 people, the gap is wide because of the minimum. At 10 people, the two are within about $120 a year on yearly billing.

Remember what each price includes. Everhour's Team plan includes integrations, expenses, time off and SSO, which Paidlyo doesn't offer. Paidlyo includes invoicing, budgets and reports on its single plan, which Everhour also lists on Team. If you'd use Everhour's extra features, the comparison is closer than the table suggests.

Also check how Everhour counts seats for people who only view reports, since every seat counts towards the bill. Our guide on [how much time tracking software costs](/guides/how-much-does-time-tracking-software-cost) covers seat rules across more tools.
sections.4.heading: A month of billing in Paidlyo
sections.4.body:
Here's what billing looks like for a 3-person web studio that moved from Everhour to Paidlyo.

Each person tracks time with the timer in a browser tab, or fills in the weekly timesheet at the end of each day. Every entry has a client, a project, a task and a billable flag. Internal work, such as studio admin and sales calls, is tracked as non-billable so it shows in reports but never reaches an invoice.

Rates are set on each project: $120 an hour for development, $105 for design and $85 for project management. One client has a 40-hour monthly cap, set as a **budget**, so the owner can see when they're close.

At month end, the owner opens the unbilled time report and creates each client's invoice in one click, grouped by task. The draft can be edited, with the studio's logo, tax and the client's currency. Clients receive a private link and open the invoice without an account.

When payments arrive, the owner records them, including partial payments. The outstanding invoices report shows which clients are late and by how long.

Without a project tool in the middle, there's nothing to keep in sync: the work happens wherever it happens, and the hours live in one place. For more on how live tracking works, see [the timer](/features/timer).
sections.5.heading: Switching from Everhour
sections.5.body:
There's no import from Everhour. Paidlyo's importer reads Harvest CSV files only, so switching is a clean start:

1. **Pick a start date,** ideally the first day of a billing period.
2. **Export your Everhour data** for your records, including past hours and reports.
3. **Bill any remaining hours** from Everhour, so nothing tracked there is lost.
4. **Add your active clients** in Paidlyo, with their currencies, and upload your logo.
5. **Create projects and tasks** with rates and budgets.
6. **Invite the team,** and tell them where to track from the start date.

If you remove an Everhour integration from your project tool, let the team know, so nobody keeps starting timers in the old place out of habit.

Remember that Everhour's annual payments aren't refunded for unused months, so time the switch close to your renewal date if you're on yearly billing.

Paidlyo costs $9 per person a month, or $90 per person a year, with every feature and unlimited clients, projects and invoices. The 14-day trial needs a card to start, and nothing is charged until it ends.
faq.1.question: How much does Everhour cost?
faq.1.answer: When we checked, Everhour Team was $8.50 per seat a month billed yearly, with a 5-seat minimum. The free plan covers up to 5 seats with limited features.
faq.2.question: Does Everhour have a seat minimum?
faq.2.answer: Yes. Everhour's pricing page said Team seats are billed at a minimum of 5, even with fewer users.
faq.3.question: Does Paidlyo integrate with Asana or Jira?
faq.3.answer: No. Paidlyo has no integrations. Time is tracked directly in Paidlyo with a timer or weekly timesheet.
faq.4.question: Is Paidlyo cheaper than Everhour for a small team?
faq.4.answer: For teams under 5, usually yes, because Paidlyo has no seat minimum. It costs **$9 per person a month**.
